name: claude-skills
description: A collection of Claude Code skills and plugins.

plugins.name: data-analysis-review
plugins.description: Empirical, objective review of a data science project: independently re-derives findings from raw data and code, then checks whether the project's own stated conclusions hold up. All analysis -- including code execution -- runs against a disposable copy of the project, so the original is never modified.

plugins.name: ciso
plugins.description: Organizes work toward security certifications (HITRUST CSF, SOC 2 Type II, ISO/IEC 27001:2022 and CMMC) alongside the development work that satisfies them. Action-oriented verbs -- register, interview, review a PR, attach evidence, audit readiness -- tracked via persistent local HTML dashboards, an index across every supported certification plus one page each. Ships structural control metadata, plus verbatim requirement text only where the publisher's work carries no copyright (CMMC's NIST and eCFR sources); licensed requirement wording is imported per-org at runtime and never stored in this repo.

plugins.name: docs-warden
plugins.description: Keeps repository documentation consistent and honest. Scaffolds a universal document set scaled by repo archetype, audits existing repos for missing, stale, or off-standard docs, enforces append-only architecture decision records, offers to archive the oldest of them into a digest once fifty are decided, and regenerates the generated ones so drift from the code is reported rather than discovered. Ships a plain-English Vale style alongside it, and a domain-model skill that maps a repo's concepts, their relationships, and which document describes each, in Python, JS/TS, PowerShell and Terraform, plus optional compliance overlays for IEC 62304, the OSPS Baseline, the EU Cyber Resilience Act and NIST SSDF, each describing document structure only and never inventing regulatory content.

plugins.name: fabflows
plugins.description: Routes work from an expensive lead model to tool-scoped workers (explorer and researcher on Haiku, editor and test-runner on Sonnet, refuter and investigator on Opus) and makes the lead re-verify their reports. using-fabflows is the session entrypoint and standing opt-in to fabflows:build, a deterministic loop in which an Opus builder implements a spec and a fresh reviewer returns ACCEPT or REWORK. brainstorming turns a rough idea into that spec: the lead asks bounded rounds of questions with recommended answers, workers read the codebase and the web, and the refuter attacks the draft lens by lens. fabflows-setup points the repository at GitHub Issues, Jira or Linear in a committed .claude/fabflows.json, so specs live in tickets instead of docs/specs/. The ticket skill keeps the ticket current through its MCP tools, and the ticket.js hook requires a Refs trailer on commits, a Spec trailer once the spec is approved, and the key in the PR title; at session start it reminds Claude to close tickets, or ask before cancelling them, whose PR merged or closed outside the session. trace writes an audit trace report outside the repo: each merged change with its PR approvers, ticket, approved spec hash, Compliance section and flags such as no-ticket or self-approved. An ACTIVE guard hook asks before package installs and runners such as npx and denies them in workers, letting through a pypdf install into a literal scratchpad --target with --isolated; it also blocks commits and pushes to a default branch, destructive commands (including ones written into a Makefile, npm script or shell script) and credential-file reads and writes. It fails open: a bug degrades to no guard, never a blocked session.
